title: The normalized ordinary ringed square at a sheaf
statement: Let $(C,J),(D,K)$ be small sites, $R_X,R_Y$ commutative coefficient-ring sheaves, $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(J),R_X)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(K),R_Y)$ a ringed-topos morphism [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], and $A$ any sheaf of sets on $(D,K)$. There exists normalized ordinary square data [def-sbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-ordinary-data]: the ringed morphism on the element-site presentations of the slices at $A$ and $f^{-1}A$, its normalized inverse-image localization comparison, and natural module isomorphisms $f_A^*r_Y\cong r_Xf^*$ and $r_Yf_*\cong f_{A*}r_X$ which are mates. The underlying direct-image comparison is the geometric mate, and the structural ring map is the restriction of the original one. No derived functors or resolution preservation data are asserted.

proof.text: Use the element-site equivalences and exact restrictions of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction]. Put $L=f^{-1}$ and $V=f_*$. The arrowwise functor $L_A:\mathscr Y/A\to\mathscr X/B$ preserves finite limits and has a right adjoint by [lem-sfb-left-exact-left-adjoint-slices]. Explicitly its right adjoint sends $p:H\to B$ to $A\times_{VB}VH\to A$, using $\eta_A:A\to VLA=VB$. Indeed, adjunction identifies a map $LK\to H$ over $B$ with a map $K\to VH$ whose composite to $VB$ is $\eta_A$ after $K\to A$; this is exactly a map into that pullback over $A$. Thus $L_A$ is the inverse image of a geometric morphism $f_A$. Since $L$ preserves products, $L_A(A\times F\to A)=(B\times LF\to B)$, naturally in $F$. This is the commutation isomorphism of the localization square.

Restrict the structural ring map $c:LR_Y\to R_X$ to $\mathscr X/B$. The last identity of step 1 identifies its domain with $L_A(R_{Y,A})$, so it gives $f_A$ its ringed structure and makes the square commute as a square of ringed topoi. Let $O=LR_Y$ on $\mathscr X$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] to the localization $j_B$ with coefficient ring $O$, to the $O$-modules $R_X$ and $LM$. Its structural ring map is an isomorphism, hence its module pullback is restriction. Together with step 1 this identifies
$$f_A^*r_YM=R_{X,B}\otimes_{r_XO}r_XLM\ \cong\ r_X(R_X\otimes_O LM)=r_Xf^*M.$$
Call this isomorphism $\sigma_M$. It preserves the scalar-extension insertion $m\mapsto1\otimes m$, since the tensor comparison is the canonical one. The module adjunctions used here are those of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction].

For an $R_X$-module $E$, restriction corresponds to the module object $B\times E\to B$. Step 1 gives
$$f_{A*}r_XE=A\times_{VB}V(B\times E)\cong A\times VE=r_Yf_*E.$$
Here $V(B\times E)\cong VB\times VE$: maps into either side are pairs of maps by the original adjunction. Addition is addition in $VE$ on each fibre. The scalar action is the action induced by $c$, restricted to that fibre, hence agrees on both sides by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Write $\delta:r_Yf_*\xrightarrow{\sim}f_{A*}r_X$ for this natural identification. If $a:M\to f_*E$ has ordinary adjunct $\widetilde a:f^*M\to E$, then the adjunct of $\delta_E r_Ya$ is $r_X\widetilde a\,\sigma_M$. To check it, first apply the slice-adjoint pullback formula of step 1 to the underlying set-sheaf transpose: it is $r_X$ of the original transpose. The module adjunct extends that map from $1\otimes m$ by $s\otimes m\mapsto s\widetilde a(1\otimes m)$, by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction, lem-weil-pbc-geometric-module-transport]. Since $\sigma$ preserves these insertions, the two extensions are equal.
